Amelia — thanks for the clear scope. We can execute this. High level plan below; we should confirm a maintenance window for the operation (non-disruptive, but we will pause related cache replication for a short period).

Planned steps:
1) Ingest the CSV and map identifiers to request IDs in our prompt-output index.
2) Run targeted KV/prefix purge for identified keys (prompts & outputs) and then invalidate any related KV cache entries.
3) Delete inference logs (request/response pairs) older/newer as matched to the request IDs.
4) Rotate any short-lived keys used for rerouting to ensure no persistent references.
5) Produce an evidence bundle: runbook, deletion manifest, per-ID checksums, and a signed execution log.

Estimated time to complete after sign-off: 48 hours. We will provide an interim status update within 6 hours of start and a final delivery with evidence once complete.

Questions for you:
- Confirm the CSV is exhaustive and whether we should also include any related session IDs (if present).
- Do you require a DocuSign-signed attestation from Redwood? We can provide either a standard deletion certificate or execute a signed acknowledgement template.

Next steps: once you confirm, I'll route to Ops (Marcus) for scheduling and to Neha for legal/compliance review.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
(attachments: hh_sanitization_plan.pdf)

Subject: RE: Request: Complete sanitation of prompts/outputs/logs (HH-472) — ops runbook

Team — taking ownership on the Ops side. I reviewed the CSV Amelia attached. Quick ops notes and runbook excerpt below.

Runbook (summary):
- Pre-checks (15m): verify cold/hot cache distribution for Helios org id; snapshot current manifests; notify monitoring to mute transient alerts.
- Execution (1–2h): for each request_id -> execute delete_prompt_output(request_id) which performs: remove prompt record from PromptStore, delete OutputStore blob, invalidate KV cache prefixes; then mark request_id as PURGED in internal index.
- Logs pruning: delete AuditLogs entries (inference namespace) where request_id in set; ensure S3 lifecycle is updated for affected prefixes.
- Post-checks (30m): compute manifest of deleted keys, generate SHA256 list, and sign manifest with operator key; store evidence bundle in a locked bucket and produce a downloadable link.

Compliance note (Neha): we will capture operator_id, UTC timestamps, and the pre/post SHA256 manifest. Recommend adding a redaction step for aggregated metrics that may contain identifiers — I will not touch metrics until legal signs off.

Attachments: sanitization_playbook.md (internal), hh_sanitization_plan.pdf (sent to customer).

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
